newsitem.title: TURKEY: Moody's seeks radical economic action from Turkey.
newsitem.headline: Moody's seeks radical economic action from Turkey.

text.p: Moody's Investor Service said it may lower Turkey's credit rating if the government does not take radical economic measures, the state-run Anatolian news agency reported on Wednesday.
"If strong economic measures are not taken we will consider whether to lower its credit rating," Moody's Turkey desk chief David Larson was quoted as telling Anatolian.
He said Moody's was currently satisfied with its Ba3 rating for Turkey, but it would be looking closely at the government's budget and other economic proposals.
"Currently, we are not thinking of changing Turkey's credit rating," he said.

Separately, Anatolian reported Turkish State Minister Ufuk Soylemez as saying he had received indications during talks with the International Monetary Fund that it would support Turkey in its planned stability programme.
Since coming to power three months ago, the government has introduced a series of revenue-raising measures aimed at reining in the country's considerable budget deficit.
